title: WiFi-Radar-for-SLAM: ambient WiFi for vehicular multipath SLAM (Sionna RT simulation + ESP32 hardware)
description: Code, configurations, result files and ESP32-S3 firmware for the study "Can Ambient WiFi Support Vehicular Multipath SLAM? Virtual-Anchor Localization, Commodity Front-End Limits, and a Delay-Convention Pitfall in Ray-Traced Evaluation". Ray-traced channels (Sionna RT 2.0.1) in three outdoor scenarios are evaluated against wheel-grade odometry with a virtual-anchor FastSLAM back-end and a LiDAR baseline. With exact multipath parameters, ambient WiFi reduces odometry drift by 66-79 %; a commodity four-element joint-MUSIC front-end returns only about 15 % facade reflections, about a third unexplained detections and 19-34 % front/back-folded paths, making WiFi-aided SLAM worse than dead reckoning. Access-point positions must be known to sub-metre accuracy. This version corrects earlier releases (v0.1.0-v0.7.1): those drove the estimator with ground-truth odometry, used a measurement update without position information, and read first-arrival-referenced CSI delays as absolute path lengths; their localization-parity, robustness, fusion, cost, phantom-ceiling and learned-discriminator results are withdrawn. PROJECT.md in the archive is the authoritative record and lists the exact commands that regenerate every number.
